text:
Rhea: Quick live thread from today's eng roadmap Q&A — focusing on runtime perf: microbatching fairness, per-tenant controls, and kernel rollout safety. Post short questions and we'll reply.
Omar: Will per-tenant batching be route-level or tenant-level? We have endpoints mapping many tenants to one route.
Rhea: Route-level opt-in in v1 (annotations), tenant-scoped policies will follow. We chose route-first to keep rollout simple.
Lucas: Any perf delta when we shard batching by route? Concerned about increased tail latency.
Nina: In our perf tests, route-sharding added a small tail bump under extreme mix (p99 +8ms). But noisy-tenant isolation reduced jitter overall.
Kai: Does that mean we should prefer isolated pools for noisy tenants?
Nina: Yes — isolated_pool + small max_batch works best for noisy/latency workloads.
Omar: Can you share a minimal policy example to paste into infra?
Rhea: Sure, small example: 

```
annotations:
  batch.policy: low-latency
  batch.max: "6"
  batch.max_wait_ms: "10"
  batch.prewarm: "enabled"
  pool.type: isolated
```

Use as starting point.
Lucas: About kernel prewarm: how do we avoid blowing memory with kv-cache prepopulation?
Nina: Prewarm will be size-limited and respect model cache caps. We'll expose prewarm_rss_delta telemetry and a per-model cap. Default prewarm sizes are conservative.
DeployBot: Canary: kernel-prewarm v2 started at 1783210100, 4/5 nodes healthy.
Kai: Is prewarm compatible with quantized kernels (q4_*), and does CPU fallback benefit?
Nina: Yes for q4 and fp16. CPU fallback will pre-compile but provides smaller improvement; still useful for CPU-only fallbacks.
Omar: If a new kernel regresses p99, what's safety?
Rhea: Auto-fallback: routing controller will detect p99 regressions and roll affected traffic to previous kernel binary after threshold. We'll also have an ops runbook and one-click rollback.
Lucas: Will SDKs need header changes?
Rhea: No RPC changes. Controls via headers + infra. SDKs will add helpers in the next patch.
Kai: Any plan for customer canaries? We want to try with one enterprise customer.
Rhea: Dedicated will create an opt-in canary pool. PM/SE will coordinate access.
Nina: Telemetry plan: per-route p50/p95/p99, prewarm_hits, prewarm_time_ms, cache_evictions, per-tenant token-cost sampling. Sampling begins next week.
Omar: Request: add a short test script for load testing (wrk or hey) that targets first-token latency and kv-hit-rate.
Rhea: Noted — we'll publish a test harness + sample prompts tomorrow.
DeployBot: Canary update at 1783210240: 5/5 nodes healthy, observed median first-token -48ms on long-context traces.
Rhea: Thanks all. Ill capture action items and follow up with owners. If you want early access to the canary, DM me. :raised_hands:
